A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same star-domain conjecture and Starlight study. All pages, including both versions' appendices, are readable, and the equations, experiments, tables and figures can be matched despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original connectivity experiments on CIFAR and ImageNet, parameter-distance analysis, Bayesian model averaging and model-fusion results.

after.justification: V2 retains original connectivity and application results and reports additional architecture, optimizer, permutation-matching and sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects the permutation-update trigger from k mod m = 0 to (k−1) mod m = 0, matching the epoch-start timing already described in v1's prose. The interpolation objective, weight matching, uniform sampling and model-fusion loss remain unchanged. This is a pseudocode correction; an implementation change is not established.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate image classification on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and ImageNet-1k; ImageNet already appears in v1 Appendix B. V2's additional architectures, optimizers and sampling experiments do not introduce new datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: V2 adds an evaluated Sinkhorn-rebasin comparison on VGG19/CIFAR-10 (Appendix C.3, Figure 6), whereas v1 only discusses that method as prior work. Table 2 also adds the best individual ensemble member as a comparator. The existing regular-model and ensemble comparisons remain.

E3.justification: V2 adds training-loss and training-accuracy evaluations as its principal evidence while retaining test results in Appendix C.1. New configurations include VGG11/19, WideResNet width/depth sweeps and Adam-source star models with 10 source and 5 held-out models. New experiments vary interpolation resolution, model sample sizes and interpolation sampling distributions.

E4.justification: V2 adds tests of sensitivity to width/depth, interpolation resolution, held-out sample size, permutation matching and uniform versus Beta versus constant interpolation sampling (Figure 2, Appendices B–C). V1's parameter-distance analysis and Table 1 disappear. Its SGD-star-to-Adam connectivity analysis remains in Appendix C.2.

E5.justification: V1 already reports standard deviations and variability across five held-out models. V2 additionally specifies three random-seed runs for the sampling ablation, reports barrier minima/maxima across different model sample sizes, and identifies best-of-three star results. These extend statistical reporting without establishing a general increase in repeated runs or introducing formal significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 adds training/test summary tables, architecture and optimizer results, sensitivity outcomes and best-model accuracies. For example, Table 3 newly reports VGG11 test barriers of 0.000 for star–regular versus 0.242 for regular–regular. V1's distance results are removed, while its model-fusion mean accuracies are retained. Training-loss replacements for test-loss plots are not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: V2 reformulates both conjectures with width and probability conditions: convexity requires width h, while star connectivity is conjectured above αh. Threshold-based solution/LMC definitions become approximately-zero formulations. New Appendix E defines average barriers, assumes monotonicity and inverse-width scaling, and derives w*=αwr conditionally; it does not prove the general conjecture.

C1.justification: V2 reframes the central contribution around connectivity below the widths required for convexity, replacing v1's broadly stated star-domain claim with a width-conditioned, probabilistic conjecture. The introduction also qualifies existence language as empirical evidence. Model fusion is newly highlighted in the abstract but was already a contribution in v1.

C2.justification: V2 interprets width experiments as supporting reduced width requirements and Adam-source experiments as suggesting star connectivity beyond SGD solutions. It adds qualifications about Sinkhorn compatibility/tuning and interpolation-sampling tradeoffs. V1's explanation that small Euclidean-distance differences cannot account for connectivity is removed. Both versions acknowledge nonzero barriers and the absence of a general proof.

D1.justification: Appendix A expands from a brief ResNet recipe and batch-normalization handling to model-specific training schedules, normalization, implementation links, FFCV use, GPU hardware, runtimes and the 11-point barrier calculation. These are substantial reproducibility disclosures, not evidence that retained experiments changed settings. V1's explicit count of 30 ImageNet models is no longer stated.

R1.justification: V2 adds substantive positioning against Annesi et al.'s perceptron star connectivity, Lin et al.'s concurrent star-model work, Ferbach et al.'s theory and Sharma et al.'s simultaneous connectivity. It distinguishes its permutation-aware, arbitrary-solution claims from these results and removes the Lubana mechanistic-connectivity discussion. This materially revises the novelty context.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work and conjecture narrative are substantially rewritten around width requirements. Method explanations are condensed and reordered, empirical discussion is reorganized, and the earlier cross-optimizer analysis moves into the appendix. The appendices are restructured into implementation, statistical checks, ablations, additional results and theoretical justification.

P2.justification: V2 changes the main text from two columns to one, redraws and relocates the schematic, restyles interpolation plots, adds summary/ablation displays and expands the fusion table while removing the distance table. Presentation errors are introduced: Figure 1's direct curve labels conflict with its caption, and Figure 5 mixes training-loss and test-loss descriptions.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens empirical support and reproducibility through width/depth tests, matching and sampling controls, and detailed implementation recipes that address important gaps in v1. The qualified conjecture and discussion of directly related star-connectivity work improve scientific positioning. These gains outweigh the removed distance analysis and plotting-label inconsistencies, although Appendix E remains conditional reasoning rather than a general proof.
